exercises.instruction: Answer the questions in the scene with too or enough + the word in brackets.
exercises.scene:
Each question, with the word you need in brackets (read the descriptions):
Does Sophie have a driving licence? (old)
I need to talk to you about something. (busy)
Let’s go to the cinema. (late)
Why don’t we sit outside? (warm)
Would you like to be a politician? (shy)
Would you like to be a teacher? (patience)
Did you hear what he was saying? (far away)
Can he read a newspaper in English? (English)

exercises.instruction: Make one sentence from two. Complete the new sentence using too or enough + to … .

items.prompt: I can’t drink this coffee. It’s too hot.
answers: This coffee is too hot to drink.

items.prompt: Nobody could move the piano. It was too heavy.
answers: The piano was too heavy to move.

items.prompt: Don’t eat these apples. They’re not ripe enough.
answers: These apples aren’t ripe enough to eat.
These apples are not ripe enough to eat.

items.prompt: I can’t explain the situation. It is too complicated.
answers: The situation is too complicated to explain.

items.prompt: We couldn’t climb over the wall. It was too high.
answers: The wall was too high to climb over.

items.prompt: Three people can’t sit on this sofa. It isn’t big enough.
answers: This sofa isn’t big enough for three people to sit on.
This sofa isn’t big enough for three people (to sit on).

items.prompt: You can’t see some things without a microscope. They are too small.
answers: Some things are too small to see without a microscope.
Some things are too small to be seen without a microscope.
